generatedProse.concept-context: In the School of Sport, reflecting through the cycle is how a session, a placement or a project becomes professional learning. Take one episode, a coaching session you led, a PE lesson you taught, or a training block you planned, and move it through the four modes rather than filing it as done. Coaching and physical education lean heavily on this. Professional bodies for coaches expect reflective practice, and Kolb's cycle gives you a way to produce it rather than leaving reflection to chance.
generatedProse.worked-example:
Two sport coaching students each lead a session that goes badly, and each writes a reflection on it.

Tom writes that the session went poorly, that he felt flustered, and that he will try to do better next time. Every sentence is about how he felt, and the one lesson is vague. The reflection stops between experiencing and reflecting: there is no thinking that explains why it went badly, and 'do better' names no action. Nothing has been transformed.

Amara sets out what happened: her warm-up overran and the players were restless by the main drill. She reflects on why: she had not timed the session plan and let one activity drift. She thinks it through, linking it to what she had read on session design and time on task. Then she acts: next time she will plan each phase to the minute and watch the clock. The reflection moves through all four modes, so the setback becomes a usable lesson.

Both students had the same difficult session. Only Amara took it round the cycle, which is what turned it into learning.
generatedProse.summary: Reflecting through the cycle in the School of Sport means taking one real episode, a session, a placement or a project, and moving it through all four modes. You cover what happened, why, what it means against what you have read, and what you will do differently. The order helps but is not a rule; what matters is that every mode is reached. You can now structure a reflection and see what each stage contributes. The last lesson turns it into an account that meets how this learning is assessed.

check.body: In the worked example, what did Amara do that Tom did not?

items.text: Thought the session through against what she had read and named a specific action.
Described the session in more detail.
Wrote the reflection in the correct fixed order.

feedback.correct: That's right. Amara reached the thinking and acting modes, which Tom never did.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Look for the modes Tom's reflection never reached.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Amara thought the session through and named an action, reaching the thinking and acting modes. More detail, feelings, or a fixed order were not the difference.
